purpose: Search tags or subjects for an attributable study. Use documented to identify the source's claims and studioUse for an original exercise. Inspect visualStudy only where an actual image was seen.
rightsPolicy: link_only means linked for study. No third-party images, thumbnails, transcripts, builds or texture files are included. A public URL does not establish a reuse license. Any code license noted applies to the named repository.
evidence: An inspected gallery image or thumbnail supports observations about its visible composition only. Technique, authorship and weathering causes require independent documentation. A null field records an unobserved or unresolved feature.

entries.creator: BdoubleO100
entries.title: Build Texture Breakdown · Building with BdoubleO #5
entries.documented: The episode revisits a mountain build to discuss texturing.
entries.studioUse: Group a facade into roof, plaster, timber and foundation before comparing individual blocks.
entries.limits: Thumbnail is promotional. Exact blocks, actual shadow source and the episode's spoken techniques were not verified.

visualStudy.composition: A large front-facing gable on the left and smaller connected roof on the right step down toward the open horizon.
visualStudy.dominantPalette: Cream panels, dark brown framing, gray footings and olive vegetation.
visualStudy.shadow: Dark beams outline the pale triangular end wall.
visualStudy.highlight: The pale upper panels and opening through the base have the strongest light shapes.
visualStudy.temperature: Warm sunset near the right horizon shifts against the blue upper sky.
visualStudy.transitions: A gray lower story and earth terraces mediate between the timber house and grass.
visualStudy.clustering: Timbers repeat as connected lines. Small flowers sit in groups along the lower edge.

entries.creator: BdoubleO100
entries.title: The Big Gate Dungeon · Hermitcraft Season 9
entries.documented: Creator identifies the Big Gate dungeon. Calven separately indexes a Big Gate study at 10:36.
entries.studioUse: Test the gate from the uphill path. Leave enough empty sky or cliff around the portal for its outline to read.
entries.limits: Thumbnail cannot separate block color from lighting or determine which stones make the shadow.

visualStudy.composition: A monumental gate fills the left side and merges into a receding hillside. A low stepped approach leads to the portal.
visualStudy.dominantPalette: Muted gray stone and yellow-green terrain against an open cyan sky.
visualStudy.shadow: A tall, nearly black opening stands between darker vertical jambs.
visualStudy.highlight: The pale gray piers read against the darker cliff and doorway.
visualStudy.temperature: Cool gray-blue distance recedes behind warmer olive ground.
visualStudy.transitions: The structure softens into similarly valued mountain stone around its edges.
visualStudy.clustering: Dark ribs repeat vertically in the gate; the field reads as much larger green masses.

entries.creator: BdoubleO100
entries.title: The Castle is DONE! · Hermitcraft Season 7 #39
entries.documented: The creator presents the completed castle and works on an interior.
entries.studioUse: Read the roof group from across the valley before choosing foreground details.
entries.limits: Only the left panel of the thumbnail was studied. Ground-level weathering and interior blockwork are unresolved.

visualStudy.composition: A dense group of tall volumes rises from a broader, simpler wall above stepped terrain.
visualStudy.dominantPalette: Gray lower walls, warm upper stone and blue-green roofs.
visualStudy.shadow: Repeating dark vertical divisions separate the towers.
visualStudy.highlight: Warmer upper faces separate the skyline from the blue background.
visualStudy.temperature: Teal roof tops contrast with warmer upper facades.
visualStudy.transitions: The narrow spires rise out of a largely continuous roof field.
visualStudy.clustering: Turrets group around a taller central mass; the lower gray section is comparatively quiet.

entries.creator: BdoubleO100
entries.title: Double Betrayal · Hermitcraft Season 8 #2
entries.documented: The episode description identifies work on the Moon base interior. Calven indexes a Season 8 Moon base segment at 5:51.
entries.studioUse: Start an organic landmark with a recognizable profile. Test whether the interior still supports movement after carving the shell.
entries.limits: No Moon base frame inspected here. Neither an exact palette nor a curvature method was verified.

entries.creator: BdoubleO100
entries.title: The Seed of Whimsy! · Hermitcraft Season 9
entries.documented: The primary episode identifies the Seed of Whimsy. Calven explicitly identifies the Tree of Whimsy at 9:08.
entries.studioUse: When studying the completed tree, first trace trunk lean, branch forks, canopy masses and gaps beneath them.
entries.limits: The primary thumbnail depicts a dark passage. It does not establish the mature tree's crown, palette or branch technique.

entries.creator: Calven, studying work by BdoubleO100
entries.title: The Secrets behind BDoubleO100 · Builders Research #1
entries.documented: Calven calls the analysis a personal interpretation. Published chapters include Moon base (5:51), castle (7:45), Tree of Whimsy (9:08) and Big Gate (10:36).
entries.studioUse: Use chapters as pointers for comparing an organic landmark with a gateway and a group of towers.
entries.limits: Calven's commentary is a secondary source for Bdubs' decisions. Chapters alone cannot establish exact block IDs or the creator's intent.

entries.creator: The Loosest Of Gooses
entries.title: Color Theory In Minecraft · All Lessons
entries.documented: Chapters cover value, hue/saturation, local color, contrast, temperature and harmony. The creator corrects an inversion: white produces a tint and black produces a shade.
entries.studioUse: Compare candidate blocks by value at distance, then judge the warm or cool cast next to their actual neighbors.
entries.limits: Chapter and description study. Specific example images, resource packs and placements were not verified.

entries.creator: Shovel241
entries.title: World Edit 101 · Brush Gradients
entries.documented: The indexed creator video identifies a WorldEdit brush gradient tutorial. The creator also references it in a custom-tree tutorial.
entries.studioUse: Compare hand-directed brush placement with a seeded field on the same wall sample.
entries.limits: Direct video fetch failed here. No commands, brush settings or visual result were verified.

entries.creator: Shovel241
entries.title: Creator channel · fantasy windmill and steampunk castle
entries.documented: Creator channel lists a steampunk castle and a fantasy windmill.
entries.studioUse: Compare the distance at which a fantasy landmark's identifying silhouette remains legible.
entries.limits: No frame of the listed castle was studied. The separate Rubyrock gallery card carries both Shovel241Builds and Graysun marks.

entries.creator: The Bakery Creators
entries.title: Bakery Creators gallery and roster
entries.documented: The gallery lists Paintergigi, Snarple, Shovel241, Ara and TheLoosestOfGooses among its creators. The Bakery describes its hub as a group build.
entries.studioUse: Use one image and its credits per comparison. Compare the focal contrast of two buildings with different silhouettes.
entries.limits: Roster membership does not identify the author of every adjacent thumbnail.

entries.creator: Gallery published by The Bakery. Card bears Shovel241Builds and Graysun marks.
entries.title: Rubyrock Fortress · presentation image
entries.documented: The Bakery displays this titled presentation card.
entries.studioUse: Keep repeated red roofs in one family. Use a cooler foundation to support a lively timber upper story.
entries.limits: The two marks are visible; the division of building, rendering and publishing credit is unverified. Studio lighting on the neutral backdrop affects visible hue.

visualStudy.composition: A tall right tower and shorter left spire bracket a broad red gable. Stacked projections widen the upper house above deep stone arches.
visualStudy.dominantPalette: Burgundy roofs, warm timber and cream plaster above blue-gray masonry.
visualStudy.shadow: A large cool mass sits on the right of the base. Dark openings pull the arches forward.
visualStudy.highlight: Pale upper faces and selected warm timber edges are brightest.
visualStudy.temperature: Warm wood and crimson roofs stand above distinctly cooler lower stone.
visualStudy.transitions: Brown posts and galleries overlap the stone, joining the upper and lower color families.
visualStudy.clustering: Red repeats in several roof caps while almost none appears on the quiet stone base.
visualStudy.focalPoint: The warm projecting gable framed by red roof and towers.
visualStudy.weathering: A little greenery touches the lower opening. The image does not establish the cause of stone discoloration.

entries.creator: Graysun, credited on the card. Gallery published by The Bakery.
entries.title: Fenwitch Cabin · terrain presentation
entries.documented: The gallery and card identify the Fenwitch Cabin.
entries.studioUse: Reserve the strongest warm accent for a single opening and let connected foliage carry the roof silhouette.
entries.limits: Image colors describe the finished render. The luminous opening's block IDs and light source are unknown.

visualStudy.composition: A low diagonal stair leads from water to a cabin, while a hooked roof mass curves over its lit upper opening.
visualStudy.dominantPalette: Leaf and moss greens, brown timber and cool blue water.
visualStudy.shadow: Dark timber under the roof and the deck contrasts with the blue distance.
visualStudy.highlight: A small amber ring is brighter than the broad roof and foreground.
visualStudy.temperature: Warm timber and isolated yellow light advance against the cool blue-violet background.
visualStudy.transitions: Hanging growth links the curling roof to the surroundings. The deck steps down toward the water.
visualStudy.clustering: Yellow is confined to one focal mass; green repeats in connected roof and bank patches.
visualStudy.focalPoint: The round glowing opening below the roof curl.
visualStudy.weathering: Hanging vegetation suggests a damp setting. No verified moisture simulation or material recipe.

entries.creator: Paintergigi
entries.title: Creator portfolio · Haunted House and Fairview Farms
entries.documented: Paintergigi describes building houses and landscapes and lists Haunted House and Fairview Farms.
entries.studioUse: Compare how a building's approach and surrounding terrain support its intended mood.
entries.limits: No named work on this page was visually scored here.
entries.rights: Creator states personal use only for builds, with redistribution and commercial use prohibited. Catalog links to the public portfolio.

entries.creator: BuildsByAra
entries.title: Minecraft architecture · creator profile
entries.documented: Ara describes creating Minecraft builds for supporters. The Bakery links Ara's architecture account.
entries.studioUse: Use a creator-approved exterior reference to compare roof-to-wall proportions and the interval between openings.
entries.limits: The public profile confirms authorship and activity. No specific example, file, palette or lesson was inspected.

entries.creator: Snarple and the participating Bakery builders
entries.title: Creator portfolio · The Bakery Hub
entries.documented: Snarple credits around 30 builders and describes coordinating the Bakery Hub.
entries.studioUse: Evaluate which landmarks orient a person at successive points on a walk. Record where another building eclipses the intended focal point.
entries.limits: Group work requires project- and image-specific attribution. The hub was not visited for this study.

entries.creator: PearlescentMoon
entries.title: Terraforming Tango... And Pickles · Hermitcraft 10 #16
entries.documented: The creator describes terraforming her solarpunk base and Tango's starter base across the river.
entries.studioUse: Check the intermediate ground between water and grass. Offset ledges and interrupt the boundary with vegetation.
entries.limits: The thumbnail includes text and avatars. Study only the landscape visible in its middle and lower right.

visualStudy.composition: A small architectural mass rises above an irregular bluff; shore and rock form a diagonal approach from the lower right.
visualStudy.dominantPalette: Blue water, pale sand, gray cliff and green mossy or grassy surfaces.
visualStudy.shadow: Dark openings between rock outcrops break up the face.
visualStudy.highlight: Bright pockets of sand line the water.
visualStudy.temperature: Pale sand mediates between the cool blue water and the greener slope.
visualStudy.transitions: Sand bends around separate outcrops; the top edge varies between exposed gray and vegetation.
visualStudy.clustering: Sand and stone form recognizable masses across neighboring blocks.
visualStudy.focalPoint: The roofed structure above the cliff in the landscape portion.

entries.creator: GoodTimesWithScar
entries.title: Scarland GRAND OPENING! · Hermitcraft 9 #46
entries.documented: The episode presents the opening of Scarland. Episode 44 separately covers the entrance build.
entries.studioUse: Study whether the arrival route keeps the dominant opening visible, and which decorative accents compete for attention.
entries.limits: Thumbnail contains an avatar, ticket, arrow and other graphic overlays. Park-wide sightlines were not measured.

visualStudy.view: architecture behind the creator thumbnail overlays
visualStudy.composition: One broad central opening and cupola are framed by lower wings and smaller domes.
visualStudy.dominantPalette: Cream walls, green roofs and gold accents.
visualStudy.shadow: The deep opening and shaded roof undersides separate the arches from the facade.
visualStudy.highlight: Pale columns and gold caps pick out high points.
visualStudy.temperature: Warm cream frames cooler green rooftops against blue sky.
visualStudy.transitions: Repeated changes in roof height draw the eye to the taller center.
visualStudy.clustering: Green and gold repeat as grouped caps. The walls carry comparatively broad pale surfaces.
visualStudy.focalPoint: The central arch and dome in the architectural layer.

entries.creator: Eaglz24 for ArdaCraft
entries.title: Gradient Guide
entries.documented: The guide compares two limestone arrangements whose connected textures change their apparent edge values. It develops a Byzantine chapel from a plain massing model before applying surface patches.
entries.studioUse: Test a limestone pairing in a wall large enough to see several texture variants. Inspect its boundary while squinting and from an angle.
entries.limits: ArdaCraft uses Conquest textures. Block names, coordinates and connected-texture transitions will differ with a vanilla resource pack.

entries.creator: ArdaCraft contributors, image published by ArdaCraft
entries.title: Rivendell · landscape view
entries.documented: The project labels the image Rivendell and credits its building work to a contributor community.
entries.studioUse: Give the higher ridgeline the quieter silhouette when vegetation and a large landmark share a valley view. Repeat an earth tone near the architecture to tie it to the hillside.
entries.limits: The building is small in this view. Individual stone IDs, wall weathering, and the source of its lighting cannot be established.

visualStudy.composition: Light cliffs and cloud wrap around a green valley. A terracotta-colored cluster of steep roofs sits below and right of center.
visualStudy.dominantPalette: Pale gray cliffs, olive and deep green vegetation, rusty red-brown roofs.
visualStudy.shadow: Dark foreground trees at the lateral edges frame the distant architecture.
visualStudy.highlight: The high rock faces and low clouds carry the palest broad values.
visualStudy.temperature: Warm foliage and rusty roofs come forward against cooler shadowed rock and sky.
visualStudy.transitions: Irregular crowns break the straight boundary between cliffs, wooded slopes and masonry.
visualStudy.clustering: Trees gather into larger color masses; the repeated roof pitches form one readable red-brown cluster.
visualStudy.focalPoint: The warm building group is the color focal point, with the bright ridgeline as a secondary pull.

entries.creator: ArdaCraft contributors
entries.title: Bree · settlement reference
entries.documented: Bree is a named project location. ArdaCraft also lists it along the route documented in Follow Frodo’s Path.
entries.studioUse: Gather street-level references before adapting eave heights, roof rhythms and changes in street width to a smaller settlement.
entries.limits: Village dimensions and a wall palette were not sampled here.

entries.creator: WesterosCraft documentation contributors
entries.title: Building fundamentals · Gradients
entries.documented: The guide prioritizes value, hue and then texture when ordering stones. It explains how skipped tones and scattered isolated patches interrupt an otherwise continuous facade.
entries.studioUse: Choose intermediate stones before painting irregular regions of decay. Check whether their scale suits the width of the whole wall.
entries.limits: The tutorial assumes the project's block collection. Verify all color matches in the active pack.

entries.creator: WesterosCraft documentation contributors
entries.title: Repository World
entries.documented: The world organizes architectural examples by region and type and includes general components and a block test area.
entries.studioUse: Index an original Studio wall or gate by region, scale and site constraint so the player can find it again.
entries.limits: The organizational idea transfers independently. Third-party builds and reference worlds were not imported.

entries.creator: Conquest Reforged
entries.title: Gradienting your Builds
entries.documented: Successive tones bridge contrasting colors in the guide's wall diagrams. Its roof discussion connects gradients and moss to the paths that rain takes.
entries.studioUse: Place a drip where water could collect and give its boundary an intermediate material. Inspect a roof at its actual pitch.
entries.limits: The examples use a custom pack. Exact texture adjacency and moss shades will vary across packs.

entries.creator: Enginnx resource index and individually credited contributors
entries.title: Minecraft Building Resources
entries.documented: The index links lessons on color and design, roof and road diagrams, site planning and terrain. It credits TheLoosestOfGooses and WhaleInThePond for the block color collection.
entries.studioUse: Consult one relevant topic at a time. For a gate approach, compare the road's movement, the landmark's silhouette and the nearby terrain before choosing individual stones.
entries.limits: This is a curated index. The diagram, video and image authors have separate rights and some credits are incomplete.

entries.creator: MasterianoX, published by Blockbench Wiki
entries.title: Minecraft Style Guide
entries.documented: The guide treats texture, shape and proportion together. Its entity workflow groups shaded pixels to show material and removes unintended banding.
entries.studioUse: Translate the principle of readable pixel groups to blocks on a facade. Review at normal play distance before adding detail.
entries.limits: Model and pixel-art conventions apply at different scales from a building. Lighting directions recommended for an entity texture are not a world lighting model.

entries.creator: Moulberry and Axiom documentation contributors
entries.title: Axiom documentation · Gradient Painter
entries.documented: Axiom's tool manual includes a Gradient Painter, Gradient Helper, Script Brush and tool masks.
entries.studioUse: Use the manual painter for a player's local corrections and inspect them through the Studio adapter before the next revision.
entries.limits: Documentation access does not establish an automation API, code reuse grant, or bundled right to distribute the mod.

entries.creator: eztaK_red and Zeranny
entries.title: ezEdits · WorldEdit/FAWE extension
entries.documented: The authors document vector-based gradients, noise controls, palette commands and light-oriented texturing.
entries.studioUse: Compare the way the tool separates a spatial mask from an ordered palette. Prototype an effect on a small bounded region.
entries.limits: Published commands describe a separate extension. Availability in this Fabric instance, licensing for reuse and practical speed were not tested.

entries.creator: Auburn and FastNoiseLite contributors
entries.title: FastNoiseLite · portable noise library and preview
entries.documented: Repository lists multiple value, simplex and cellular algorithms, domain warping and fractal options, with JavaScript and other language ports.
entries.studioUse: Compare two frequencies on one fixed facade and seed; rank candidates by continuity and fit to the intended weathering. Use a mask tied to the structure for physical effects.
entries.limits: The library supplies fields rather than architectural decisions. Studio's current painterly pass uses its existing noise sampler.
entries.rights: Repository code is MIT. Viewer linked for study. No library code bundled by this catalog.

entries.creator: paulprints and project contributors
entries.title: MCPalletePicker · image-to-block palette
entries.documented: README describes texture-derived colors, seeded OKLab clustering of reference pixels and matching colors to blocks. It also documents block families and shape filters.
entries.studioUse: Extract candidate colors from an authorized image. Test neighboring blocks as actual masonry, including grain, seams and strength of contrast.
entries.limits: An image-derived color match does not infer where to put its blocks or whether an installation has the same textures.
entries.rights: Repository code is MIT. Source images and Minecraft textures retain their separate rights. Link only.

entries.creator: Shape Craft
entries.title: Block Palette Generator & Color Matcher
entries.documented: The site documents color matching, gradient stops and image clustering in OKLab. Filters include falling blocks and light sources.
entries.studioUse: Use a perceptual match as an initial shortlist, then reject materials whose states, light emission or texture seams conflict with the wall.
entries.limits: Site functionality was reviewed from its own documentation. Accuracy on the active resource pack and any API or reuse license are unverified.

entries.creator: EngineHub / WorldEdit contributors
entries.title: WorldEdit patterns
entries.documented: The manual documents weighted and uniform random block patterns for selections.
entries.studioUse: Keep a weighted-random wall as the control when evaluating a clustered weathering field.
entries.limits: Expected material proportions do not guarantee a coherent patch shape.

entries.creator: GDMC Settlement Generation Challenge organizers
entries.title: Settlement evaluation methodology
entries.documented: The organizers describe human evaluation of generated settlements on unseen maps using adaptability, functionality, narrative and aesthetics.
entries.studioUse: Review a player's route as well as a distant image. Record a concrete observation for each criterion before judging a treatment.
entries.limits: This is a settlement evaluation framework. It gives no specific palette or geometry algorithm.

entries.creator: GDPC contributors
entries.title: Generative Design Python Client
entries.documented: The project identifies itself as a Python client for the GDMC HTTP Interface.
entries.studioUse: Study how surveying an area before planning can expose constraints for a road or settlement approach.
entries.limits: This is an external reference; this catalog makes no compatibility claim for Studio's running game.

entries.creator: Minecraft World Studio project
entries.title: Registered tower · varied overhead-shadow test
entries.documented: The capture belongs to the project's registered tower test. The accompanying test receipt records the material revision.
entries.studioUse: The dark upper region still spans much of the facade. A critique can ask whether retaining more midtone would keep the eave from dominating the slit windows.
entries.limits: This test fixture is above the cloud layer. Terrain integration and ground weathering cannot be judged from this shot.
entries.rights: Existing project capture linked in place. Minecraft assets remain subject to their respective rights.

visualStudy.composition: The narrow tower stands alone with sky around the shaft; the small stepped roof flares beyond its sides.
visualStudy.dominantPalette: Muted green roof and charcoal-to-gray masonry.
visualStudy.shadow: Dark courses directly under the eave have an uneven lower edge.
visualStudy.highlight: Lighter shaft stone sits beside the dark slits and below the eave region.
visualStudy.temperature: Green-gray stone forms a quieter step between green roof and neutral gray shaft.
visualStudy.transitions: Dark patches descend by different distances in adjacent columns.
visualStudy.clustering: Upper dark blocks form a mostly continuous cap. Lower slit streaks are much narrower.
visualStudy.focalPoint: The green roof and dark band below it.
visualStudy.weathering: Narrow marks below slit openings follow the previously tested drip mask.

entries.creator: Minecraft World Studio project
entries.title: Registered bridge · weathered downstream view
entries.documented: The existing bridge-weathering test records sampled water height and changes near the footings.
entries.studioUse: Compare both banks from water level and from the approach. Check whether the pale high masonry separates the span from the forest at play distance.
entries.limits: A tree obscures part of the left bank. The dark recess high on the slope also competes for attention.
entries.rights: Existing project capture linked in place. Minecraft assets remain subject to their respective rights.

visualStudy.composition: The span cuts diagonally across blue water. Sloped banks and trees frame the crossing.
visualStudy.dominantPalette: Gray masonry against green foliage, brown banks and blue water.
visualStudy.shadow: Darker gray-green blocks collect near the base of the right support.
visualStudy.highlight: Pale faces along the upper masonry separate the steps from the hill.
visualStudy.temperature: Cool masonry and water contrast with the exposed earth on the slope.
visualStudy.transitions: Darker footing stones meet intermediate gray courses before the pale upper faces.
visualStudy.clustering: The lower accents form small connected groups while the tread remains quiet.
visualStudy.focalPoint: The arch opening and pale bridge face.
visualStudy.weathering: Dark right footings meet the water. The material receipt establishes the waterline-based placement.
